# CoCAD

> CoCAD is a free, MIT licensed desktop app for OpenSCAD models on Linux, Windows and macOS. An AI agent changes the model over MCP, and the window builds it again. The Optimize tab prepares the parts for the printer and shows a layers preview. The app exports STL, 3MF and STEP, and the Render tab makes path traced photos.

OpenSCAD does the geometry through its CLI, so the user must install OpenSCAD too. CoCAD needs an OpenSCAD development snapshot (nightly) with the Manifold backend. The 2021.01 release does not have Manifold. Get a snapshot at https://openscad.org/downloads.html#snapshots. When CoCAD finds no snapshot, the window shows the install steps.

The Section bar at the top right of the 3D view cuts the view across X, Y and Z in all tabs. The export does not use the cut. The right panel has three tabs: Model (build, parts, explode, mesh check), Optimize (print preparation and the layers preview) and Render (path traced photo). Export 3MF at the bottom of the Optimize tab writes the print plate as 3MF. Its menu writes the plate as STL, all plates with one file each, or the model as STEP. A 3MF of a plate has one object for each print part. The Model menu has the export commands too.

The Optimize tab puts the print parts on one or more plates and counts parts with the same shape. Custom orientation is off by default: Auto puts a part on its best face, or the user selects the face. The print fixes are teardrop holes, hole size for vertical holes, bridges, bed chamfer, a brim on small bed islands and mouse ears on the sharp bed corners of large parts. All fixes are off until the user turns them on, and they change the exported mesh. The Check card lists overhangs, long bridges, arcs in bridges, small islands and parts that are too large for the bed. For a part that is too large, CoCAD proposes a split with a flat, pins or dovetail joint. Parts with the OpenSCAD `%` mark are reference parts: they show in gray and are not printed or exported. File > Settings > Printer has presets and the default print area.

The layers preview is not a slicer: it has no travel moves or supports, and it writes no G-code. Usage analytics and error reports are optional, and each stays off until the user accepts it.

## Docs

- [Website](https://cocad.cgeosoft.com/): Overview, the agent loop, the Optimize tab, MCP setup and downloads
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cgeosoft/cocad/main/README.md): Short overview with links to the wiki
- [Wiki](https://github.com/cgeosoft/cocad/wiki): Install, first steps, each feature, the CLI and the build steps
- [Optimize tab](https://github.com/cgeosoft/cocad/wiki/Optimize): Plates, orientation, print fixes, the check, the split and the layers preview
- [Model definition](https://github.com/cgeosoft/cocad/wiki/Model-definition): The `<model>.yml` file next to a `.scad` model, with the title, the part names and colors, and the parameter sets
- [Model definition schema](https://cocad.cgeosoft.com/schema/model-1.json): JSON Schema of version 1 of the `.yml` file
- [Releases](https://github.com/cgeosoft/cocad/releases): Downloads and release notes

## MCP

- [AI assistant](https://github.com/cgeosoft/cocad/wiki/AI-assistant): Client setup
- [MCP reference](https://github.com/cgeosoft/cocad/wiki/MCP-reference): Setup, the tool list and the behavior

The client runs `cocad mcp` as a stdio server. Tools: `get_state`, `get_params`, `get_source`, `view_model`, `open_model`, `new_model`, `set_params`, `reset_params`, `build` (the old name `render` also works), `get_optimize`, `set_optimize`, `slice`, `export_model`, `save_photo`, `set_view`, `load_parameter_set`, `save_parameter_set`, `list_windows`, `select_window`.

## Optional

- [Source code](https://github.com/cgeosoft/cocad): Rust, egui and an own OpenGL renderer
- [Privacy Notice](https://cocad.cgeosoft.com/privacy/): What the desktop app and the website send, who receives it and how long it stays
